title: Teaching
text: I teach courses in microeconomic theory, introductory economics, and the history and development of economic thought at Hunter College and the Graduate Center, CUNY. Below are selected course materials and resources that I use in teaching.

title: Teaching
text:
Graduate Microeconomic Theory
My graduate microeconomics materials emphasize strategic interaction, information, and computational approaches to economic theory.

Microeconomics II
Topics include principal-agent problems, bargaining, global games, adverse selection, and related applications of game theory.
Micro II Sandbox

title: Teaching
text:
Introductory Economics
For introductory economics at Hunter, I use a variety of examples, data, graphical exercises, and supplementary materials to connect basic economic models to real-world questions.

ECO 100 — Introduction to Economics
Jonathan Conning has assembled a useful collection of notes and teaching resources for ECO 100 at Hunter.
ECO 100 Resources

title: Teaching
text:
Development of Economic Thought
This course examines the development of economic ideas in their historical and intellectual context, from early political economy through the development of modern economics.

History of Economic Thought Resources
The History of Economic Thought Website is an extensive reference for economists, schools of thought, original texts, essays, and related historical material.
History of Economic Thought Website

title: Matthew J. Baker
text:
A deliberately simple site
This is meant to be easy to maintain. A new paper can be added with a title, a two-line description, and links to the paper, appendix, code, or replication files. No database or web editor is required: edit a .qmd file, render, and push to GitHub.

title: Research
text:
Forthcoming publications

A Model of Enclosures: Coordination, Conflict, and Efficiency in the Transformation of Land Property Rights
Matthew J. Baker and Jonathan Conning · 2026
Review of Economic Studies, forthcoming.
A model of the transformation of common-property regimes in which private enclosure decisions can be strategic complements or substitutes, with implications for coordination, conflict, and efficiency.
Online appendix and replication materials


Cultural Transmission, Property Rights, and Treatment of the Elderly
Matthew J. Baker and Joyce P. Jacobsen · 2026
Journal of Population Economics, forthcoming.
A model of how property rights, production technologies, and cultural transmission interact to shape the treatment and economic position of the elderly.
